note: The frame-time and input-latency gate (scripts/frame-gate.mjs; premium-feel recs R2 and R5). target: the recs' bar (a frame's script time p95 under 16.7 ms on the laptop profile and 33 ms on the phone, no frame over 100 ms, an input answered within 100 ms and 150 ms); a measure past it is reported, never blocking. fail: the ceiling that blocks a pull request in ci.yml (checks.yml only warns). CI's runners draw in software and the profiles slow the page 4x and 6x on top, so what they measure is far above the bars; the ceilings are set from what they measured, to catch a regression and not to say a bar is met. The first set (31 Oct, from checks run 1105, one sample each: 66 ms p95 on the phone, 250 ms the longest frame) was below what untouched code measured there, so it would have blocked every merge. Now: a scenario's own ceiling (scenarios) is its measured number x1.5 for a script p95 and an input, x2 for the longest frame; the generic ceiling covers a scenario nobody has measured yet (the laptop's pinch, glide, slide change and inputs did not report on 31 Oct: the run was cut off at its time limit). Tighten each to the number the runners report next, with the same margin, and never loosen one to get a run through. Times in ms.
